source.title: Mechanistic Knobs in LLMs: Retrieving and Steering High-Order Semantic Features via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Ruikang Zhang; Shuo Wang; Qi Su

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Extends feature-retrieval and feature-steering analysis to an LLM setting, testing whether an SAE can recover behaviorally relevant sparse features in a language model. It does not test the original toy-model geometry or capacity account.
record.gate_note: The paper uses an overcomplete SAE and discusses sparsity, but does not measure feature overlap, interference, neuron polysemanticity, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition. Layer and steering-coefficient choices are setup details, not results. CAA is a comparator for steering performance, not a test of the claim's representational units.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained SAE (Llama-Scope-R1-Distill) as a tool to retrieve personality-related features in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B. It reports how well its own retrieval-and-steering method works: TRAIT scores, valid rates, comparison with CAA, and SocialEval shifts. It does not measure superposition, feature overlap, interference, neuron polysemanticity, or whether the SAE recovers the model's representation, and does not compare SAE features with neurons. Features were kept only if steering produced monotonic behaviour, so their steerability is a selection result, not a test of V4 or V5. V5's completeness, stability and canonicity are not examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors also claim the retrieved features are largely monosemantic. They claim that steering them shifts SocialEval behaviour in patterns matching human personality psychology ('Functional Faithfulness'), and that their method beats CAA on polarity and validity. They note the effects carry benefit-tradeoff costs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature retrieval, activation injection, and personality benchmarks in an instruction-tuned LLM rather than testing the original toy-network superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Trait and polarity change the measured TRAIT scores. The paper also reports that CAA's performance and generation validity vary by trait, but CAA is a comparator rather than an SAE-feature result.

fits_no_version.finding: Single SAE latents, chosen by contrastive activation frequency and steering monotonicity, shift TRAIT personality scores bidirectionally (e.g., Neuroticism 0.2117 to 0.4412/0.1017) with little loss of valid rate. Openness barely moves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected SAE features in an 8B LLM act as causal steering handles for high-level personality traits.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.2: a feature with a large input-activation contrast (about 13.6x) had little effect on output when steered.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features that correlate with an input concept are not necessarily causally used for output.

record.problems: Evidence is from one 8B model and selected representative features. Figure 2 provides activation patterns without numerical values. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Its results do not establish SAE feature completeness, canonicality, or generality across models.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. CAA comparator results and SocialEval task results are not included because they do not directly test the claim's representation-geometry or canonical-unit assertions.

untested.parts: No toy models; no geometry, interference or sparsity transition.
No study of neuron polysemanticity or capacity.
No study of causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons; no assessment of whether the SAE recovers sparse features beyond the five hand-selected, steering-validated features.
No test of completeness, stability across SAEs or seeds, or canonicity of SAE features.
Features are defined as single SAE latents; dimensionality is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: This is a steering-method paper that uses SAEs as a tool, with one representative feature per trait in one model. Its features were filtered for steering effect, so reading the results as evidence for V4/V5 would be circular. The reader's V4/V5 supports labels are removed. The study gives no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, interference, or sparsity-dependent geometry in toy networks.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from feature competition or limited capacity.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Tests SAE-recovered personality-related features in one model; does not test feature spreading across many neurons or generalize across LLMs.
Tests selected SAE features as functional intervention targets, but not whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across models, training runs, or dictionaries.

Defines an SAE feature as one latent dimension and intervenes on decoded feature vectors, but does not test whether represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected Big Five personality features in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
reader_labels.reason: The reported activation patterns and feature-based intervention results support recovery of sparse, behaviorally relevant SAE features in this tested model (r1-r5, r11-r20).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected SAE features and TRAIT benchmark in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
reader_labels.reason: Several selected-feature interventions shift trait scores in the intended polarity while Valid Rates remain high, supporting their usefulness as functional intervention targets (r11-r30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Selected features for the five traits in the single tested model
reader_labels.reason: The evidence concerns selected features and one model; it does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical representation units (r1-r5, r11-r30).
